title: Improving the estimation of spin-bath parameters via initial correlations and a two-qubit probe
authors: Anila Khan, Huzaifa Amjad, Rizwan Abbas, Ali Raza Mirza
abstract: We study how a second qubit can improve the estimation of spin-environment parameters when only one of the two qubits is measured. Both qubits are coupled to a common spin bath through the exactly solvable central-spin model, in which populations and coherences both evolve. Because the bath operator coupled to the qubits commutes with the bath Hamiltonian, the environment induces no effective interaction between the qubits. Without initial correlations or direct inter-qubit coupling, the two-qubit probe therefore performs exactly like a single qubit. When initial system-environment correlations are included, preparing the second qubit reshapes the environment statistics in a parameter-dependent way, and the measured qubit reads out this imprint. This improves the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the coupling strength by factors of 3-4 relative to a correlated single-qubit probe, and by more than an order of magnitude relative to an uncorrelated one. For temperature estimation, the improvement reaches a factor of about 8. A direct Ising coupling does not help by itself, but the advantage persists in its presence. We also derive the classical Fisher information for arbitrary projective measurements and identify the measurement that saturates the QFI, which in general lies out of the equatorial plane of the Bloch sphere.
summary: This paper demonstrates that using a two-qubit quantum probe, when initialized with specific correlations with the environment, significantly enhances the precision of estimating spin-bath parameters compared to using a single qubit or an uncorrelated two-qubit setup. The improvement stems from the second qubit reshaping the environment's statistical imprint, providing a powerful tool for quantum sensing.
main_problem: The paper aims to improve the precision of estimating spin-bath parameters (like coupling strength and temperature) by utilizing a two-qubit quantum probe.
main_result: Including initial system-environment correlations allows the two-qubit probe to significantly enhance the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) compared to single-qubit or uncorrelated two-qubit probes, achieving gains of factors of 3-8.
method: The analysis uses quantum metrology techniques, specifically calculating the Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and Classical Fisher Information (CFI) for parameter estimation.
model_or_system: The system consists of a two-qubit probe coupled to a common spin bath, modeled by an exactly solvable central-spin Hamiltonian. The dynamics are analyzed using the reduced density matrix formalism.
key_observables: Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) and Classical Fisher Information (CFI) are the primary diagnostics used to quantify estimation precision.
